<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/particles.js@2.0.0/particles.min.js"></script>

  <div class="ms-hero">
    <span class="ms-tag">Paleoclimate · Research</span>
    <h1 class="ms-title">Palaeoclimate Research at University College London</h1>
    <div class="ms-meta-row">
      <span>🏛️ University College London</span>
      <span>📍 London, United Kingdom</span>
      <span>📅 2018</span>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="ms-body">

    <div class="ms-main">

      <p class="ms-desc">After completing my PhD, I joined one of the world's leading research universities to work at the intersection of palaeoclimate science and computational modelling. UCL's Department of Geography is home to some of the most respected palaeoclimate researchers in Europe, and joining that environment — even for a year — was a formative experience.</p>

      <p class="ms-desc">The project focused on stalagmites as climate proxies. Stalagmites grow inside caves over thousands of years, and their chemical composition records past changes in temperature, rainfall, and atmospheric circulation. By simulating how stalagmites grow, we can reconstruct what the climate looked like long before instrumental records began.</p>

      <div class="ms-callout">
        <p>Working at UCL meant attending interdisciplinary project meetings in London and Reading, collaborating with geologists, isotope chemists and climate modellers, and learning to communicate across very different scientific cultures. It also pushed my Python skills in a new direction — building physical simulations from scratch rather than postprocessing model output.</p>
      </div>

      <h2 class="ms-subtitle">What I did</h2>
      <ul class="ms-list">
        <li>Developed a Python model to simulate stalagmite growth behaviour from first principles</li>
        <li>Built a comprehensive database of speleothem proxy climate records</li>
        <li>Wrote scientific reports and contributed to project documentation</li>
        <li>Attended research meetings in London and Reading with interdisciplinary teams</li>
      </ul>

      <h2 class="ms-subtitle">Tools & methods</h2>
      <div class="ms-chips">
        <span>Python</span><span>Proxy climate data</span><span>Stalagmite modelling</span>
        <span>Palaeoclimate reconstruction</span><span>Speleothem analysis</span>
      </div>

    </div>
